body: I could not reproduce this with the latest NewRelic agent

Hitting this weird IAE in CL.definePackage - but in code that's not even dealing with Quarkus, but Weld 6 for testing purposes.

The IAE is thrown for rather random packages (from my app).

With a debugger: before the call to `packages.putIfAbsent(name, p)` in `j.l.ClassLoader.definePackage()`, the package name is absent - but nonetheless that `putIfAbsent` yields a _different_ non-`null` `Package` instance.

Adding (a ton of) breakpoints in `j.l.c.ConcurrentHashMap` (writes to `val` and the calls to `Unsafe`) didn't yield any useful information. Also adding a breakpoint in the `NamedPackage` constructor didn't help. Even adding breakpoints to `j.l.reflect.ReflectAccess#newInstance` watching for dynamic constructions of a `Package` object yielded nothing.

I don't really understand why the `Package` instance created in `definePackage()` is not the one that is later contained in `packages`. At this point, I'm running out of ideas.

The actual is the _concurrent_ definition of packages via concurrent class loading (explicit via `Class.forName()` et al or implicit via "lazy" class initialization doesn't matter). With Weld, the issue does not manifest with `org.jboss.weld.bootstrap.concurrentDeployment=false`.

But whether it's Quarkus or Weld does not matter. Every application can hit this issue - just the probability to hit this issue varies.

There are some related OpenJDK issues: [JDK-4302423](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-4302423) [JDK-4841786](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-4841786) [JDK-6832540](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-6832540). The issue itself is not new, but the code in `j.l.ClassLoader.definePackage()` is still fundamentally the same:
```java
if (packages.putIfAbsent(name, p) != null)
  throw new IllegalArgumentException(name);
```

As the mentioned OpenJDK issues are resolved/closed/stale, I've opened [JDK-8349545](https://bugs.openjdk.org/browse/JDK-8349545)

Thanks @snazy.

I'll close this here as there doesn't seem to be anything Quarkus can  do
@geoand I think the only thing that Quarkus could do is to catch the `IllegalArgumentException` and retry. I doubt that the observed behavior of `definePackage` (and its call sites) will change soon.
Sounds reasonable to me, but here is where @dmlloyd comes up with some super deep technical argument on why that might not be a good idea :)

Actually, while there are additional subtleties to consider like locking behavior, that is essentially the correct solution (catching and retrying). The prototype new class loader does in fact work in this way.

Cool, thanks @dmlloyd!

@snazy would you like to contribute  the proposed fix?

issue.title: Retry when `CL.definePackage()` throws an IAE

labels.name: area/devtools
labels.description: Issues/PR related to maven, gradle, platform and cli tooling/plugins

issue.body:
`java.lang.ClassLoader.definePackage()` succeeeds if, and only if, the package was not already defined. This is problematic when packages are defined concurrently, for example when classes are loaded concurrently. `j.l.ClassLoader` does not offer something like `definePackageIfNotExists()`.

The proposed fix here is to change the implementations of `definePackage` in in `io.quarkus.bootstrap.classloading.QuarkusClassLoader#definePackage` and also `io.quarkus.launcher.RuntimeLaunchClassLoader#definePackage`, the same change was applied by #42139 to `io.quarkus.bootstrap.runner.RunnerClassLoader#definePackage`:
1. check if the package is already defined via `CL.getDefinedPackage()`
2. if it is, then return
2. if not, then call `CL.definePackage()`
3. if the former fails with an `IllegalArgumentException`, then check once against `getDefinedPackage()`, rethrow the IAE, if the pacakge's not defined

I could not find another `ClassLoader` implementation in Quarkus, which could be prone to IAEs via `CL.definePackage()`'s behavior.

Fixes #37363
